assessment.verifiedEvidence: Checked the question text, all 4 choice symbols and the official answer ロ against the official original drawing. ⑦ is the dashed box in the lower left of the lighting panel wiring diagram. It connects the 100V 20A BE to the 6 remote-control relays. The primary source for the symbol meanings could not be read.

Primary source: https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/law/409M50000400052/20230320_504M60000400096 (the body is JS-rendered, so I read the same text through the e-Gov API: https://laws.e-gov.go.jp/api/1/articles;lawNum=平成九年通商産業省令第五十二号;article=58). Article 58 of the ministerial ordinance on electrical equipment technical standards, table: 300V or less with voltage to ground of 150V or less, 0.1MΩ; other cases 0.2MΩ; over 300V, 0.4MΩ. This supports every choice explanation. The original drawing confirms that ⑧ points to the double-circled g circuit in the lower left of the plan, and that the lighting panel wiring diagram shows double-circled g as 200V 20A (BE→TS). The official answer イ matches.

explanationIssues: The line 'the lighting loads on double-circled a–f include single-phase 200V circuits' is inaccurate. The drawing marks all six circuits, double-circled a through f, as 200V 20A single-phase 200V circuits. Write that they are all single-phase 200V circuits.

The claim that a single-phase 200V circuit needs a 2-pole relay that switches both poles has no stated basis. Add the reason: in a single-phase three-wire system, both wires of a 200V circuit are ungrounded (100V to ground each), so both must be switched. Add a source for this too.
